title: arXiv Mathematics daily notable papers — 20 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred, evidence-weighted selection, not a readership ranking; citation evidence is sparse for papers announced today and independent expert attention was not established in the checks.

sections.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
sections.abstract: The authors prove amplitude-dependent wave-envelope estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions and derive sharp small-cap decoupling for dimensions n ≥ 4, resolving the Demeter–Guth–Wang exponential-sum conjecture in all dimensions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove amplitude-dependent wave-envelope-type estimates and use them to establish sharp small-cap decoupling for the moment curve in every dimension n ≥ 4; they state this completes the Demeter–Guth–Wang conjecture on exponential sums across dimensions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The estimates concern the moment curve; the new small-cap theorem is stated for dimensions n ≥ 4 and uses prior sharp square-function estimates.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a preprint claim; its main argument depends on the cited square-function estimates, and the full proof has not been independently assessed here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports an all-dimensional conjecture resolution, with new sharp small-cap estimates for n ≥ 4; its proof builds on sharp square-function estimates, giving a specific mathematical basis for prominence.

sections.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
sections.abstract: For continuous and affine maps from high-dimensional simplices to R^d, the authors determine the optimal asymptotic fraction of d-faces whose images share a point, obtaining (d+1)!/(d+1)^(d+1) in every dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves c_d^top = c_d^aff = (d+1)!/(d+1)^(d+1) for every integer d ≥ 1, confirming the cited conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The constants are asymptotic minima over maps from the n-simplex to R^d as n tends to infinity; the topological case allows every continuous map, while the affine case restricts to affine maps.
sections.unique_caveat: The preprint reports that AI helped discover the proof under the author's direction. The linked Lean formalization is described as based on an earlier draft, so it should not be treated as a formal check of every detail of this exact version without comparing the texts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The exact formula settles the Bukh–Matoušek–Nivasch conjecture for the affine constant while matching it with the topological constant; the author also links a Lean formalization, an unusually concrete verification artifact for this result.

sections.title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
sections.abstract: For nested-arch events in the critical-percolation loop representation, the authors derive Pfaffian formulas that imply rational dependence on cylinder circumference and rational limiting probabilities in the half-plane.
sections.claimed_result: For k nested arches on a semi-infinite cylinder of circumference 2N, with k < N, the authors give Pfaffian formulas and prove rational-function dependence on N; the corresponding half-plane probabilities are rational.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The model is the completely packed O(1) loop representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice; the stated cylinder result covers k < N.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper does not establish Romik's predicted denominator properties or dyadic rationality, and excludes the boundary case N = k. The authors note that Dan Romik separately obtained a full solution with AI, to be reported in forthcoming work; that result is not established by this preprint.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper combines three subject areas and reports explicit formulas for a family of probabilities, proving key parts of a named conjecture rather than only offering numerical evidence.

sections.title: An asymptotic bound for Yuster's independent transversal factor conjecture
sections.abstract: For graphs split into r independent parts with pairwise matching edges, the author proves that a partition into independent transversals exists once the part size is at least r + O(r^(20/21)), for sufficiently large r.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves f(r) ≤ r + O(r^(20/21)) and hence f(r)/r → 1, where f(r) is the least part-size threshold guaranteeing a partition into independent transversals.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: An [r,n,1]-graph has r independent parts of size n and a matching between each pair; the theorem is for all sufficiently large r and n ≥ ceil(r + A r^(20/21)) for an absolute A > 0.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an asymptotic form, not the exact threshold in Yuster's 2021 conjecture; the stated error term remains above the conjectured linear threshold.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The bound gives a near-linear threshold and implies f(r)/r → 1, a direct asymptotic advance on a named factor conjecture; the result also crosses combinatorics and discrete mathematics.

sections.title: Permanence and 144-periodicity of x_{153,3} in the stable stems at the prime three
sections.abstract: The author proves that a class in the 3-primary Adams–Novikov spectral sequence survives and generates a period-144 family, answering both parts of a question by Carrick and Davies.
sections.claimed_result: The author shows that x_{153,3}, in stable degree 153 and filtration 3, survives and begins a period-144 family; iterates have nonzero image in the specified height-two detector.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is the 3-primary Adams–Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere; the argument uses comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on possible differential targets.
sections.unique_caveat: The detector and permanence argument establish the claimed family in this specific 3-primary setting, not a general periodicity statement for stable stems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper answers a stated question with both a permanence result and a periodic family, and supplies a concrete finite-spectrum lift with nonzero detector images.

sections.title: Algebraic matroids with non-algebraic duals exist in any positive characteristic
sections.abstract: The author constructs, over every positive-characteristic field, an algebraic matroid whose dual is not algebraic over any field, and uses it to separate two classes of polynomial supports.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that for every field K of positive characteristic, some matroid algebraic over K has a dual that is not algebraic over any field; realizable volume- and covolume-polynomial support classes consequently differ.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The construction applies to fields of positive characteristic and uses matroids over one-dimensional algebraic groups.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an existence result in positive characteristic; the abstract does not classify such matroids or establish the same separation in characteristic zero.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The theorem is uniform over every positive characteristic and gives a strong non-realizability conclusion for the dual; its application connects matroid theory with algebraic geometry and volume polynomials.

sections.title: Remark on Kobayashi's conjecture: a volume Schwarz lemma
sections.abstract: The author reconstructs an AI-assisted proof of Kobayashi's ampleness conjecture for compact Kähler manifolds and proves a volume comparison yielding a general-type criterion under a bounded-indicatrix hypothesis.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims that a compact Kähler manifold with nef canonical bundle and a bounded Kobayashi–Royden indicatrix at some point is of general type, as a consequence of the volume comparison.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The comparison assumes a Kähler metric with Ric(ω) ≥ −ω and uses intrinsic volume forms associated with Kähler–Einstein metrics on pseudoconvex domains containing the Kobayashi–Royden indicatrix.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract describes an expository reconstruction of an AI-assisted proof plus new results; these remain preprint claims and require expert review, especially for the conjecture-level argument and its hypotheses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper spans differential and complex geometry, states a new volume Schwarz lemma and pointwise comparison, and draws a concrete birational-geometric consequence from them.

sections.title: Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
sections.abstract: The authors give a model-independent exploration approach to arm separation for planar percolation and apply it to obtain a strong arm-separation result for critical planar FK percolation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a generic arm-separation statement for arbitrary planar percolation models by exploring conditioned configurations so exposed arms are revealed with positive probability, then derive strong separation for critical planar FK percolation.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The method concerns planar models and polychromatic arm events; the application is critical planar FK percolation.
sections.unique_caveat: Arm separation is an input to other conclusions such as quasi-multiplicativity and exponent identification; this paper's abstract does not claim those consequences follow without additional hypotheses and estimates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It provides a reusable method across planar models and a specific critical FK application, while linking probability with mathematical physics.

sections.title: Nondegeneracy and uniqueness of ground states of the Schrödinger equation with Neumann conditions in a weakly nonlocal regime
sections.abstract: For a fractional Schrödinger equation in a half-space with nonlocal Neumann conditions and fractional order close to two, the authors prove ground-state nondegeneracy and uniqueness up to tangential translation and sign.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the only solutions of the linearized equation are tangential derivatives of the ground state and conclude uniqueness up to tangential translations and sign.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The equation is driven by a fractional Laplacian of order 2s with s close to 1, in a half-space under nonlocal Neumann conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is restricted to the weakly nonlocal regime (s close to 1); the abstract gives no explicit numerical range for s.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It addresses a less-studied nonlocal Neumann half-space setting and derives both a linearized-kernel characterization and uniqueness, rather than only existence.

sections.title: Paper2Lean: Agentic Autoformalization of Mathematical Research Papers at Scale
sections.abstract: The authors introduce an agentic pipeline for turning mathematical research papers into Lean projects and report 20 optimization papers formalized into compilable projects, followed by human semantic review and repair.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that all 20 generated projects compile without proof placeholders; after human review and semantic repair, the OptPaper-20 corpus has 20 corrected formalizations, all passing clean builds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Evaluation uses 20 mathematical optimization papers, mathlib, and a shared library of supporting results; the corrected corpus is publicly linked by the authors.
sections.unique_caveat: Compilation checks formal proof terms, not whether the formalized statements faithfully capture each source paper; the reported corpus required human review and semantic repair, as the authors acknowledge.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It reports a paper-level evaluation with 20 projects and a public dataset of 494 Lean files and 110,910 lines, making the reproducible artifact a concrete signal beyond the framework description.
